summary: WI-763 implements the PR merge gate, workflow, and controlled-merge semantics, but the branch does not satisfy its own merge-checkpoint freshness contract: the authored review record at `.loom/reviews/WI-763.json` is stale for current HEAD and does not match the current `latest_validation_summary`, causing `checkpoint merge` and `pr-gate check` to fail closed. In addition, the “host-enforced” portion of the goal still lacks live GitHub readback evidence (required check enforced via branch protection/ruleset and a PR-head run).

findings.summary: `checkpoint merge` and `pr-gate check` fail closed because `.loom/reviews/WI-763.json` is stale for current HEAD and its `reviewed_validation_summary` does not equal `.loom/progress/WI-763.md` `Latest Validation Summary`; this violates WI-763 closing condition (“fresh authored review record for the PR head”) and prevents demonstrating a passing PR-head approval gate on this branch.

disposition.summary: Record a refreshed authored implementation review bound to the current HEAD and current `latest_validation_summary`, then re-run `checkpoint merge` / `pr-gate check` to confirm the gate passes for the PR head.

findings.details: Observed on HEAD `2fd4bf5fd09d867cebc6ffadab7e8d8fa917a3bd`: `python3 tools/loom_flow.py checkpoint merge --target . --item WI-763` => `result=block` with missing inputs including `review artifact does not match the latest validation summary` and `review artifact is stale for the current HEAD`; `python3 tools/loom_flow.py pr-gate check ...` also returns `result=block` for the same reasons. Review record binds `reviewed_head=9fa121df...` and `reviewed_validation_summary` referencing `... at 6b46f96`, while recovery `Latest Validation Summary` is `... at 8aef9fa`.

findings.summary: Goal requires “host-enforce” semantics, but current repo-local evidence still lacks live GitHub readback proving `loom-pr-merge-gate` is required (branch protection or active ruleset) and ran on the current PR head; without that, WI-763 cannot close the PR #762 regression class on the host platform.

disposition.summary: After pushing the PR head, record host readback evidence: required-check enforcement (branch protection/ruleset) + PR-head workflow run + controlled-merge consuming that readback.

findings.details: This is explicitly part of WI-763 `Closing Condition` and cannot be fully satisfied by repo-local workflow presence alone.

findings.summary: The required-check workflow checks out and executes repository code from the PR head (`python3 tools/loom_flow.py ...`). This preserves explicit head binding, but it is a host trust-boundary decision for repos that accept untrusted external PRs.

disposition.summary: Keep this as an explicit governance boundary; if untrusted PRs are allowed, restrict who can trigger the required check or replace the workflow body with pinned tooling / API-fetched artifacts before requiring it.

findings.details: Current workflow uses `contents: read` and `pull-requests: read`, but the primary risk is executing PR-supplied code as a required check.

findings.summary: Stock `loom-pr-merge-gate` workflow triggers only on `pull_request`; if GitHub merge queue is enabled, required checks may need `merge_group` coverage to avoid enforcement gaps or non-reporting on merge groups.

disposition.summary: Treat merge-queue compatibility as an explicit follow-up decision; add `merge_group` and validate only when Loom self-governance enables merge queue.

findings.details: WI-763 scope appears to target direct PR merges; this remains a compatibility boundary to document/decide explicitly.
